input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance. Each Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such insurance upon request
input.rationale: A usable insurance covenant exists at Section 14.6, so the rule is not missing. RevMed must procure and maintain insurance (expressly including product liability cover) appropriate to its activities under the Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements, for the whole period during which any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product is in human clinical testing or is commercially distributed or sold — i.e. coverage matched to the actual risk profile of this collaboration rather than the CGL/E&O/cyber stack contemplated by the preferred position, which is calibrated to services/hosting vendors processing Customer Data. RevMed is not a data processor or on-premises services vendor here, so walk-away territory is not engaged. The clause also delivers the key customer-side protections: evidence of insurance on request (equivalent to certificates on request), advance written notice from RevMed of cancellation, non-renewal or material change, and an express statement that the insurance does not cap RevMed's indemnification obligations under Article XIV. Two features are affirmatively in our favour and are not flagged: the self-insurance option is available to Sanofi only, and the cancellation-notice obligation runs one way against RevMed. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the clause states no dollar limits (relying on the "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" standard, which is market for this deal type) and has no express one-year tail beyond the coverage period, which is partly mitigated because the obligation runs for as long as Product is tested or sold. On its material terms the clause meets the rule's intent at the fallback level, so we are not redlining it.
